items.title: Tesla saw a significant increase in Model 3 sales in Canada during the third quarter, helped by the arrival of vehicles manufactured in Chin
items.content_excerpt: Tesla saw a significant increase in Model 3 sales in Canada during the third quarter, helped by the arrival of vehicles manufactured in China and aggressive local pricing. DesRosiers Automotive Consultants said some Model 3 versions are priced about 25% below U.S. levels, with a starting price of roughly $27,700 in Canada versus $36,990 in the U.S. The increase follows an agreement between Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping allowing up to 49,000 Chinese-made EVs into Canada over 12 months at a reduced 6.1% tariff. Previously, Chinese EVs faced a 100% surcharge introduced in 2024. Carney has said Teslas are expected to account for most vehicles entering under the quota in the short term. Government data show that nearly 16,000 EVs from China have entered Canada since May, with about half priced below $24,553. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles globally in Q3. $TSLA

items.title: Google has raised the price of its seven-month-old Pixel 10a by $100 to $599, citing higher memory costs as a persistent chip shortage conti
items.content_excerpt: Google has raised the price of its seven-month-old Pixel 10a by $100 to $599, citing higher memory costs as a persistent chip shortage continues to pressure the consumer electronics industry. The increase marks another example of rising component costs being passed on to smartphone buyers, even for older, lower-priced models. The Pixel 10a offers limited upgrades over the 2025 Pixel 9a and uses Google’s Tensor G4 processor, which was introduced two years ago. Meanwhile, Samsung has raised prices on most Galaxy S26 models by $100, while Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max also launched above their predecessors’ prices. Google’s newer Pixel 11 lineup started at $899, $100 above the previous generation, with the company adding more storage to entry-level configurations to offset part of the increase. The range reaches $1,899 for the base Pixel 11 Pro Fold, reflecting broader pressure on smartphone pricing from higher memory and component costs. $GOOGL $SSNLF $AAPL

items.title: Apple plans to introduce stronger privacy controls for Mac users as AI agents increasingly require broad access to personal files and applic
items.content_excerpt: Apple plans to introduce stronger privacy controls for Mac users as AI agents increasingly require broad access to personal files and applications. The company said developers have been using “Full Disk Access” in ways that could put users at risk, and it will require a more explicit user action before granting applications access to system files, emails, messages and browsing history. Apple said the risks will increase as AI agents become more capable and autonomous, particularly because these tools can act on behalf of users with limited human supervision. The company emphasized that users should clearly understand the privacy implications before granting such permissions. The move comes as AI agents gain adoption across the industry. OpenAI said more than 35 million people now use ChatGPT Work and Codex, up from 10 million in July, while Meta’s Muse recently topped app-download rankings. $AAPL $META $OPEAZZX.P

items.title: Amazon is exploring a deal to move roughly $8 billion worth of high-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet, according to the Financial Times
items.content_excerpt: Amazon is exploring a deal to move roughly $8 billion worth of high-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet, according to the Financial Times, as major technology companies seek alternative ways to finance the massive infrastructure spending required for AI. Under the proposed structure, thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips deployed across more than a dozen U.S. data centers would be transferred to a special-purpose vehicle funded by outside investors. Amazon would then lease the hardware back, allowing it to continue using the chips while reducing the amount of AI infrastructure held directly on its balance sheet. The special-purpose entity could issue debt and potentially sell up to 10% of its equity to investors. If it achieves an investment-grade credit rating, long-term investors such as insurers and pension funds could participate in the financing. $AMZN $NVDA $GOOGL $MSFT

items.title: $AMZN Amazon is pitching investors on an 8 billion sale-leaseback of its AI chips, per the FT. Thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips, al
items.content_excerpt: $AMZN Amazon is pitching investors on an 8 billion sale-leaseback of its AI chips, per the FT. Thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips, already running in a dozen-plus US data centers, would move into an outside-investor vehicle funded with debt. Amazon keeps up to a 10 percent equity stake and leases the chips back. One level down: this is GPUs as financial engineering. Meta already kept its Louisiana data center debt off the balance sheet through Blue Owl. The WSJ counted roughly 3 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments across nine top tech names in August, mostly AI. Amazon gets cash and a cleaner balance sheet, and the fast-depreciating hardware is no longer its problem. The catch: the vehicle's higher borrowing costs come back to Amazon as higher lease payments. Tracking which hyperscaler does the next one.

items.title: Amazon will invest more than $1 billion over five years in U.S. communities that host its AI data centers through a new “Built Together” ini
items.content_excerpt: Amazon will invest more than $1 billion over five years in U.S. communities that host its AI data centers through a new “Built Together” initiative, as the company seeks to address local concerns surrounding rapid data-center expansion. The program, announced by AWS CEO Matt Garman, will fund free university education, workforce training and energy-efficiency improvements for schools and homes. Amazon also introduced a Data Center Commitment, promising that its facilities will not increase local electricity bills and that the company will publish annual data on energy and water consumption. Garman said Amazon will also stop using nondisclosure agreements with government agencies involved in its data-center projects, a practice that has become a point of contention among local opponents. The initiative comes as hyperscalers accelerate AI infrastructure investment and face scrutiny over electricity demand, water usage and grid upgrades. . $AMZN

items.title: Amazon is exploring a deal to move roughly $8 billion worth of high-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet, according to the Financial Times
items.content_excerpt: Amazon is exploring a deal to move roughly $8 billion worth of high-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet, according to the Financial Times, as major technology companies seek alternative ways to finance the massive infrastructure spending required for AI. Under the proposed structure, thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips deployed across more than a dozen U.S. data centers would be transferred to a special-purpose vehicle funded by outside investors. Amazon would then lease the hardware back, allowing it to continue using the chips while reducing the amount of AI infrastructure held directly on its balance sheet. The special-purpose entity could issue debt and potentially sell up to 10% of its equity to investors. If it achieves an investment-grade credit rating, long-term investors such as insurers and pension funds could participate in the financing. $AMZN $NVDA $GOOGL $MSFT

items.title: Apple plans to introduce stronger privacy controls for Mac users as AI agents increasingly require broad access to personal files and applic
items.content_excerpt: Apple plans to introduce stronger privacy controls for Mac users as AI agents increasingly require broad access to personal files and applications. The company said developers have been using “Full Disk Access” in ways that could put users at risk, and it will require a more explicit user action before granting applications access to system files, emails, messages and browsing history. Apple said the risks will increase as AI agents become more capable and autonomous, particularly because these tools can act on behalf of users with limited human supervision. The company emphasized that users should clearly understand the privacy implications before granting such permissions. The move comes as AI agents gain adoption across the industry. OpenAI said more than 35 million people now use ChatGPT Work and Codex, up from 10 million in July, while Meta’s Muse recently topped app-download rankings. $AAPL $META $OPEAZZX.P

items.content_excerpt: London-based AI infrastructure developer Nscale has appointed former Meta executive Justin Osofsky as chief operating officer, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. Osofsky spent 18 years at Meta, most recently as head of partnerships, and will report directly to Nscale CEO Josh Payne while overseeing global operations. The appointment comes as Nscale accelerates preparations for a planned New York listing after confidentially filing for an IPO in September. Bloomberg previously reported that the company aims to raise up to $3 billion to purchase specialized hardware and expand data-center capacity to meet growing demand for AI computing. Nscale, spun out of a crypto-mining operation in early 2024, has rapidly expanded by leasing high-performance computing resources to AI developers and has established partnerships with Nvidia and Microsoft. $META

items.title: Google has raised the price of its seven-month-old Pixel 10a by $100 to $599, citing higher memory costs as a persistent chip shortage conti
items.content_excerpt: Google has raised the price of its seven-month-old Pixel 10a by $100 to $599, citing higher memory costs as a persistent chip shortage continues to pressure the consumer electronics industry. The increase marks another example of rising component costs being passed on to smartphone buyers, even for older, lower-priced models. The Pixel 10a offers limited upgrades over the 2025 Pixel 9a and uses Google’s Tensor G4 processor, which was introduced two years ago. Meanwhile, Samsung has raised prices on most Galaxy S26 models by $100, while Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max also launched above their predecessors’ prices. Google’s newer Pixel 11 lineup started at $899, $100 above the previous generation, with the company adding more storage to entry-level configurations to offset part of the increase. The range reaches $1,899 for the base Pixel 11 Pro Fold, reflecting broader pressure on smartphone pricing from higher memory and component costs. $GOOGL $SSNLF $AAPL

items.title: Amazon is exploring a deal to move roughly $8 billion worth of high-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet, according to the Financial Times
items.content_excerpt: Amazon is exploring a deal to move roughly $8 billion worth of high-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet, according to the Financial Times, as major technology companies seek alternative ways to finance the massive infrastructure spending required for AI. Under the proposed structure, thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips deployed across more than a dozen U.S. data centers would be transferred to a special-purpose vehicle funded by outside investors. Amazon would then lease the hardware back, allowing it to continue using the chips while reducing the amount of AI infrastructure held directly on its balance sheet. The special-purpose entity could issue debt and potentially sell up to 10% of its equity to investors. If it achieves an investment-grade credit rating, long-term investors such as insurers and pension funds could participate in the financing. $AMZN $NVDA $GOOGL $MSFT

items.content_excerpt: $SPY $QQQ $IWM Look at the monthly chart below of the 10 year yield. A bull flag pattern breakout is occuring right now. From Jan 2026, yields rallied forming an uptrend. A bull flag pole. Then there was consolidation between 4 to 5%. That created a bullish consolidation flag formation pattern. Once the consolidation ended there was a breakout. A text book bull flag breakout. The target is 6% as you can see in the chart which is also the 6.18 fibonachi level. That's major resistance. In 2 weeks the 10 year rallied 38 basis points. In the next 4 weeks yields could potentially rally a further 70 basis points sending yields to 6%. 35 basis points in the next 2 weeks. X 2 = 70. 5.3% add 70 basis points = 6%.

items.title: $QQQ There's not enough physical assets for the US to pay off its debt. The only way is to to allow high inflation for a decade to erode
items.content_excerpt: $QQQ There's not enough physical assets for the US to pay off its debt. The only way is to to allow high inflation for a decade to erode the value of the debt. Like when the U.S. used a combination of high post-war inflation, pegged low interest rates, and budget surpluses to significantly erode the real value of World War II debt. Inflation then peaked at 18%. The current U.S. national debt—which crossed $40 trillion and is on track to hit $41 trillion—is vastly larger than the post-World War II debt, both in terms of inflation-adjusted purchasing power and relative to the size of the U.S. economy. Adjusted for inflation, the WW2 debt was to roughly $4.3 trillion in today's money. Gross Debt-to-GDP Ratio ~106% to 113% for after WW2 vs. ~125% to 126% now. And now is much more of a worry as it's structural rather than temporary.

items.title: The U.S. Department of Justice said it will not reopen its criminal investigation into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the c
items.content_excerpt: The U.S. Department of Justice said it will not reopen its criminal investigation into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the central bank’s overbudget headquarters renovation. Attorney General Todd Blanche said Friday that the DOJ is not reopening the criminal probe, while leaving open the possibility of separate action if an independent audit uncovers evidence of criminal wrongdoing. The decision follows a Federal Reserve inspector general report that found no reasonable grounds to believe a federal crime occurred requiring a referral to the attorney general, although it identified significant management and oversight failures that contributed to renovation costs more than doubling. The DOJ originally opened the investigation in January and issued grand jury subpoenas for renovation-related records. A federal judge later quashed the subpoenas in March. $QQQ $IWM $SPY

items.title: $OMER Omeros is targeting enrollment by year-end 2026 in the NIDA-funded Phase 1b inpatient trial of OMS527 for cocaine use disorder. The st
items.content_excerpt: $OMER Omeros is targeting enrollment by year-end 2026 in the NIDA-funded Phase 1b inpatient trial of OMS527 for cocaine use disorder. The structure is the cheap optionality. NIDA fully funds the program. Omeros is developing its PDE7 inhibitor at the agency's request, and the preclinical interaction studies, designed with NIDA toxicologists, came back with no drug-interaction or safety issues. The gate was the FDA. It asked for additional nonclinical information before the inpatient trial, so Omeros is running that nonclinical study now to unblock enrollment. The mechanism: PDE7 inhibition modulates signaling in the brain's dopamine axis without depressing the reward system, which is the main drawback of marketed anti-addiction agents. There is no approved treatment for cocaine use disorder.

items.title: $OMER OMS527 update Omeros targets start of the NIDA-funded Phase 1b inpatient trial in cocaine users this quarter (by year-end 2026). First
items.content_excerpt: $OMER OMS527 update Omeros targets start of the NIDA-funded Phase 1b inpatient trial in cocaine users this quarter (by year-end 2026). First data expected mid-to-late 2027. Fully funded by NIDA → zero cash burn for Omeros. Clean preclinical interaction studies + solid Phase 1 in healthy volunteers. Realistic take: interesting low-risk side bet. The fact that NIDA is fully sponsoring this (one of the few programs they back this heavily) means they clearly see real potential in the PDE7 mechanism. Addiction trials are tough, but the unmet need is massive and the data so far look promising. Not a near-term driver vs Yartemlea, but a nice free option in the pipeline.

The CHMP has a strict limit of 60 calendar days to conclude its assessment and adopt a final positive or negative opinion. • Expert Consultation: As part of this current evaluation phase, Omeros requested the review be looked over by an Ad Hoc Expert Group (AHEG). This independent panel of external clinical experts is convened by the EMA to advise the committee prior to the final vote. Final Outcome Window Because the active evaluation clock runs for 60 days following the receipt of detailed grounds, the CHMP's final, definitive opinion on whether to uphold or overturn the refusal of narsoplimab is expected to be adopted during late autumn 2026 (likely at an upcoming October or November CHMP plenary meeting).

items.title: $OMER A CHMP positive decision is NOT marketing Authorisation It’s a question whether YARTEMLEA is actually on the Oct CHMP agenda or Novemb
items.content_excerpt: $OMER A CHMP positive decision is NOT marketing Authorisation It’s a question whether YARTEMLEA is actually on the Oct CHMP agenda or November’s. But if Oct, the sequence would be: * October 12–15: CHMP meets and considers the re-examination. * By the end of the meeting Oct 16, CHMP reaches its scientific opinion * Within a few days, EMA publishes the CHMP meeting outcome * OMER will presumably know by Oct 15/16 But only the EU Commission can grant the marketing-authorisation. A positive CHMP opinion would then go through the EU Commission’s formal decision process. So CHMP re-examination then CHMP opinion then EU Commission decision The EU decision is generally within 67 days or so but can vary. So, if positive CHMP decision Oct 16 then EU authorization would come about Dec 18, subject to the EU’s process. If instead a Nov CHMP decision, then EU authorization Jan 18 But regardless, it’s the CHMP decision that’s key.

items.content_excerpt: $OMER - "The Omeros MASP-2/C1inh proprietary diagnostic assay is an advanced investigational biomarker test developed by Omeros Corporation designed to detect lectin pathway hyperactivation." Core Function & Mechanism • Targeting the Lectin Pathway: Mannan-binding lectin-associated serine protease-2 (MASP-2) is the primary effector enzyme responsible for triggering the lectin pathway of the complement system. • Measuring Activation Complexes: When the lectin pathway overactivates, active MASP-2 forms complexes with C1-inhibitor (C1inh), a primary endogenous regulator. By measuring these specific MASP-2/C1inh complexes in blood plasma, the proprietary assay functions as a highly specific diagnostic tool to quantify ongoing, pathological lectin pathway activity. items.title: $IBRX The market is starting to realize IBRX is no longer a binary biotech story. Breaking $10 wasn't just another technical breakout. I
items.content_excerpt: $IBRX The market is starting to realize IBRX is no longer a binary biotech story. Breaking $10 wasn't just another technical breakout. It shattered a major resistance zone while shorts held one of the largest bearish positions in biotech. If price reaches $15 with no news, that tells us institutions aren't waiting for a PR. They're positioning ahead of what they believe is coming. At that point, the story changes completely. Every dollar higher puts more pressure on shorts, while deep out-of-the-money calls begin moving in-the-money, forcing dealers to hedge. That's how an ordinary breakout can evolve into a self-feeding squeeze. The most dangerous setup for bears is not bad news. It's no news while the stock keeps climbing. If IBRX reaches and holds $15, the question becomes "How many shorts can still afford to stay short?" Locked-up holders. Rising revenue. Institutional accumulation. Massive short exposure. That's the type of setup that can turn skepticism into panic buying very quickly.

Amazon is exploring a deal to move roughly $8 billion worth of high-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet, according to the Financial Times, as major technology companies seek alternative ways to finance the massive infrastructure spending required for AI. Under the proposed structure, thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips deployed across more than a dozen U.S. data centers would be transferred to a special-purpose vehicle funded by outside investors. Amazon would then lease the hardware back, allowing it to continue using the chips while reducing the amount of AI infrastructure held directly on its balance sheet. The special-purpose entity could issue debt and potentially sell up to 10% of its equity to investors. messages.body: $OMER Omeros is targeting enrollment by year-end 2026 in the NIDA-funded Phase 1b inpatient trial of OMS527 for cocaine use disorder. The structure is the cheap optionality. NIDA fully funds the program. Omeros is developing its PDE7 inhibitor at the agency's request, and the preclinical interaction studies, designed with NIDA toxicologists, came back with no drug-interaction or safety issues. The gate was the FDA. It asked for additional nonclinical information before the inpatient trial, so Omeros is running that nonclinical study now to unblock enrollment. The mechanism: PDE7 inhibition modulates signaling in the brain's dopamine axis without depressing the reward system, which is the main drawback of marketed anti-addiction agents. There is no approved treatment for cocaine use disorder.

$OMER OMS527 update Omeros targets start of the NIDA-funded Phase 1b inpatient trial in cocaine users this quarter (by year-end 2026). First data expected mid-to-late 2027. Fully funded by NIDA → zero cash burn for Omeros. Clean preclinical interaction studies + solid Phase 1 in healthy volunteers. Realistic take: interesting low-risk side bet. The fact that NIDA is fully sponsoring this (one of the few programs they back this heavily) means they clearly see real potential in the PDE7 mechanism. Addiction trials are tough, but the unmet need is massive and the data so far look promising. Not a near-term driver vs Yartemlea, but a nice free option in the pipeline.

$OMER The European Medicines Agency (EMA) is actively re-examining its negative opinion on Yartemlea (narsoplimab) following a formal request submitted by Omeros Ireland Limited on July 15, 2026. 🔎 Current Status • Initial Opinion: The CHMP recommended refusing marketing authorization on June 25, 2026. • Reason for Refusal: Insufficient evidence of effectiveness and an unresolved benefit-risk balance. • Re-examination Request: Filed on July 15, 2026, by the applicant. • Next Steps: Omeros is seeking a review by an Ad Hoc Expert Group (AHEG).

$OMER A CHMP positive decision is NOT marketing Authorisation It’s a question whether YARTEMLEA is actually on the Oct CHMP agenda or November’s. But if Oct, the sequence would be: * October 12–15: CHMP meets and considers the re-examination. * By the end of the meeting Oct 16, CHMP reaches its scientific opinion * Within a few days, EMA publishes the CHMP meeting outcome * OMER will presumably know by Oct 15/16 But only the EU Commission can grant the marketing-authorisation. A positive CHMP opinion would then go through the EU Commission’s formal decision process. So CHMP re-examination then CHMP opinion then EU Commission decision The EU decision is generally within 67 days or so but can vary. So, if positive CHMP decision Oct 16 then EU authorization would come about Dec 18, subject to the EU’s process. If instead a Nov CHMP decision, then EU authorization Jan 18 But regardless, it’s the CHMP decision that’s key.

Core Function & Mechanism • Targeting the Lectin Pathway: Mannan-binding lectin-associated serine protease-2 (MASP-2) is the primary effector enzyme responsible for triggering the lectin pathway of the complement system. • Measuring Activation Complexes: When the lectin pathway overactivates, active MASP-2 forms complexes with C1-inhibitor (C1inh), a primary endogenous regulator. By measuring these specific MASP-2/C1inh complexes in blood plasma, the proprietary assay functions as a highly specific diagnostic tool to quantify ongoing, pathological lectin pathway activity. messages.body: $IBRX The market is starting to realize IBRX is no longer a binary biotech story. Breaking $10 wasn't just another technical breakout. It shattered a major resistance zone while shorts held one of the largest bearish positions in biotech. If price reaches $15 with no news, that tells us institutions aren't waiting for a PR. They're positioning ahead of what they believe is coming. At that point, the story changes completely. Every dollar higher puts more pressure on shorts, while deep out-of-the-money calls begin moving in-the-money, forcing dealers to hedge. That's how an ordinary breakout can evolve into a self-feeding squeeze. The most dangerous setup for bears is not bad news. It's no news while the stock keeps climbing. If IBRX reaches and holds $15, the question becomes "How many shorts can still afford to stay short?" Locked-up holders. Rising revenue. Institutional accumulation. Massive short exposure. That's the type of setup that can turn skepticism into panic buying very quickly.
